labels.label: ersprop:PropLocUniqueness
labels.notes: Reported partial and unmarked. That is right. I read the Lean against ghd_02_19.tex:836-838 (the statement), :840-844 (the proof) and :814 (GHD; S connected). The anchor is ers_prop_4_63_globallyHyperbolicOn (ErsUnions.lean:346). Its hypotheses fall into three classes. In the paper: hG GloballyHyperbolicOn U₁ and hS IsCauchySurfaceOn U₁ S (u₁ a GHD with Cauchy hypersurface S), [T2Space M] (ℝ^{d+1}), and hglue, the reading of Causal.ErsUniqueness (solutions as an agreement predicate that glues). Named: hloc LocalUniqueness S (U₁ ⊓ U₂) agree, Sogge's DS_p ⊆ W_p ⊆ U₁ ∩ U₂ with u₁ = u₂ there and a Cauchy surface S_p ⊆ S (:841, :843). Added: hC CausallyArcConnectedOn U₁ and hext CurvesExtendOn U₁, both Lorentzian facts and both disclosed. Two hypotheses are dropped, which is a weakening: u₂ is a GHD, and S is connected. The conclusion is the paper's whole conclusion: IsCommonDevelopment (V ≤ U₁ ⊓ U₂, S ⊆ V, agreement, S Cauchy) ∧ GloballyHyperbolicOn V ∧ V causally convex in U₁, for V = localDevelopmentUnion, the union of all such D, which contains ERS's ⋃ DS_p. ers_prop_4_63 (:291) is the OQ-41 reading: S acausal in U₁, and only the antisymmetry of ≤_{U₁} is used. It concludes no GH (OQ-57 (c)). ers_prop_4_63_of_hasTimeFunction (:362) gets the two added hypotheses from CausallyArcConnected and HasTimeFunction at M. Nothing is vacuous and the theorem is not trivial. LocalUniqueness is the analytic half of ERS's proof and does not contain the conclusion. The Cauchy property of the union needs the ambient: the meeting with S is unique because S is acausal in U₁. GH needs convexity in U₁ (causallyConvexIn_of_isCauchySurfaceOn, GloballyHyperbolicOn.of_causallyConvexIn). LocalUniqueness can be supplied as stated: it asks less than the PDE gives (not p ∈ S_p, not S_p open, not GH of DS_p). The witness timelikeLine_ers_prop_4_63 is a proper instance: U₁ = ℝ and U₂ = ]-1,1[ differ, u₁ = id and u₂ = the clamp differ off [-1,1], DS_0 = ]-1/2,1/2[, and every hypothesis of the GH form genuinely holds on the timelike line. timelikeLine_not_isCauchySurfaceOn_union does show that the ambient cannot be dropped. Take B = ℝ, which is causal. The pieces ]-1,1[ ∋ 0 and ]0,2[ ∋ 1 have Cauchy surfaces {0} and {1} inside S = {0,1}, with S ∩ Dᵢ = Sᵢ. The only hypothesis that fails is 'S acausal in B' (respectively 'S Cauchy in B'). No open B ⊇ ]-1,2[ can supply it, because 0 ≤ 1 there. Its S is disconnected (finding 4). The OQ-57 (c) evidence holds. IsCommonDevelopment.globallyHyperbolicOn (:306) makes any common development GH and causally convex when U₁ is GH, S is Cauchy in U₁, and U₁ satisfies CausallyArcConnectedOn and CurvesExtendOn. It uses no Geroch. ers_remark_4_67_globallyHyperbolicOn (:320) adds 'S Cauchy in U₁' to 4.64's hypotheses, as its docstring says. The label is written without ** (:14).

labels.label: ersthm:ThmEx
labels.notes: Reported partial and unmarked. That is right. I read the Lean against :1001-1003 and the proof :1011-1022. The hypotheses of ers_theorem_4_75 (:668), by class. Reading: cau, D, u, a family of local solutions, each with its own causality. In the paper: hex, the patches cover S (p ∈ S_p ⊆ DS_p); the instances [T2Space], [LocallyConnectedSpace] and [Nonempty β] (ℝ^{d+1}, values in ℝ). Named: hdev IsLocalDevelopment, Sogge's local existence (:1011). Its fields are GH, tarentin, S acausal, SplitBy, CompactSlabs and S Cauchy in DS_p. They can be supplied from S_p by IsCauchySurfaceOn.of_subset_of_isAcausalOn, since S ∩ W_p is a slice. Named: hcomp, RestartsIn on each component, for i ≠ j. It has four fields: 'meets' (N's integral curves, :1014), local uniqueness on S ∩ A, and FrontierStaysIn and SliceRestart located in A. In the conclusion, two antecedents on Cu. Reading: Cu agrees with each cau i on the opens of D i (g(v) = g(u_p) on DS_p); it is quantified after v, so it is not circular. Added: ≤_U of Cu is antisymmetric, ers_theorem_4_77's hcaus. That is part of the paper's conclusion (finding 3). The conclusion: ∃ v with v = u_i on D i, S ⊆ ⋃ D i, and S Cauchy in ⋃ D i for every such Cu. GH of U is not concluded (OQ-57 (c)), and this is disclosed. The paper's claim, u_p = u_q on DS_p ∩ DS_q, is exactly ers_theorem_4_75_eqOn (:635), with the by-product that S is Cauchy in DS_p ∩ DS_q. The route differs from ERS. ERS use the domains of dependence D_pS_A, D_qS_A and a boundary argument. The Lean runs 4.64's argument in the component A with W = DS_p (maxDevelopmentIn_eq :414, ers_theorem_4_64_in :440). The conclusion is still the paper's claim. RestartsIn does not contain the conclusion. Its step field asks for a larger development only at a spacelike frontier point in A. That such a point exists is Step 2 (exists_isSpacelikeBoundaryPoint), which uses GH, tarentin, SplitBy and CompactSlabs of DS_p and FrontierStaysIn. The conclusion is Step 1 + Step 2 + the restart, as in Causal.ErsUniqueness. isCauchySurfaceOn_iSup_of_inf (:529) checks out. A diff against ers_theorem_4_77 (NestedCausalities.lean:1084-1178) shows one changed line: NestedCausalities.lean:1119 'exact hSU j hs₁S' becomes ErsUnions.lean:564 'exact hcσ ▸ (ordConnectedComponent_subset hσ).2.2', which reads c σ ∈ U i ⊓ U j off the meeting point, where c σ = c s₁. The signature is ers_theorem_4_77's without hSU, so hSU is unnecessary, and the kernel checks it. The witness timelikeLine_ers_theorem_4_75 is a proper instance. It has two distinct patches, ℝ and ]-1,1[, with distinct solutions, id and the clamp, and one overlap component, ]-1,1[. RestartsIn is proved for every development V of ]-1,1[ inside W = ℝ or W = ]-1,1[: stay by the geometry of the line, step with V' = ]-1,1[. The SliceRestart premise is inhabited: V = ]-1/2,1/2[ is a development in ]-1,1[ with the spacelike frontier point 1/2. So the hypothesis is not vacuous. The restart itself, though, is the by_contra branch of maxDevelopmentIn_eq, and no instance enters it. In the witness ]-1,1[ is itself a development, so Step 1 already gives maxDevelopmentIn = ]-1,1[. 'Runs non-vacuously' (REPORT notes[6]) can only mean that the premise is inhabited, which the Lean does not exhibit. Cu = timelikeLine (reflexive, causal) satisfies both antecedents of the ∀ Cu conclusion. The label is written without ** (:20).

build.details: Build: cd lean-causal && taskset -c 0-11 lake env lean -DwarningAsError=true scaffold/CausalScaffold/ErsUnions.lean gives exit 0 and no output. grep finds no sorry, admit, axiom, native_decide, implemented_by or extern. Axioms: the probe was a verbatim copy of the file plus 31 #print axioms and an env.allImportedModuleNames #eval, under campaign/T-abs-ers-unions/, and it is deleted. Every theorem gives [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], including the 20 the REPORT names; GloballyHyperbolicOn.compactSlabs_singleton gives [propext, Quot.sound]. Imports: Causal.ErsUniqueness, Causal.CBG.CausalConvex and Mathlib.Topology.Connected.LocallyConnected. The compiled closure is 34 Causal.* modules, exactly the REPORT's list, and the source-level walk gives the same 34. It contains no Minkowski, Static, Flat.*, Model.*, Port.*, SingularFlat, Splitting, LemmaK* or LevinUtility. Its only CBG module is CBG.CausalConvex. tools/ladder.py model_path is None for Causal.ErsUniqueness and for Causal.CBG.CausalConvex. No statement uses a metric notion. Name clashes: ladder.py's namespace-aware index finds 44 declared names, exactly REPORT decls ∪ extra_decls. None is declared in lean-causal/Causal or in any other scaffold file, ErsMughd.lean included. I read ErsMughd.lean as text only: its 27 names are disjoint, and none of its sources uses componentOpens, LocalUniqueness, RestartsIn, IsLocalDevelopment, IsDevelopmentIn, maxDevelopmentIn or ersWitness*. The file body elaborates under `import Causal` (all 246 strict modules) with -DwarningAsError=true and no error. A sanity probe confirmed that a duplicate name is reported. Docstring contract (kb/0006): the title is present, and the two labels appear unmarked in the first 4000 characters. The quotes of :836-838, :843, :1001-1003 and :1011-1021 match the tex. The checklist, SCOPE and Provenance are present (finding 7). Paper findings, checked against ghd_02_19.tex. (1) :843 ('It is immediate … V is globally hyperbolic with Cauchy hypersurface S') relies on the ambient. :841 requires W_p ⊆ U₁ ∩ U₂, and the meeting with S is unique only because S is acausal (Cauchy) in U₁ ⊇ V. The finding is true, and 'no error' is the right class (but see finding 4). (2) :1021 asserts that U = ⋃ DS_p is a GHD, with no argument for its Cauchy property or its GH. True: the open–closed union argument appears only in 4.77 (:1037-1044). (3) The bypass of :1014-1021 is disclosed honestly. The 'a posteriori' connectedness of A ∩ S_p ∩ S_q is at :1014, and 'The global hyperbolicity of DS_p and DS_q shows' is at :1021. (4) '4.63 never uses u₂ GHD beyond Sogge, nor S connected' is true of the Lean. Scope: git status --short shows only two paths for this closer: scaffold/CausalScaffold/ErsUnions.lean, and campaign/T-abs-ers-unions/ with only REPORT.json. programme/ladder.toml belongs to the keeper. programme/roadmap.toml has three status flips to active (T-lad-record-minimal, T-abs-ers-unions, T-abs-ers-mughd), from the master. The ErsMughd files belong to the other closer. I ran no lake build, and ErsMughd.lean was neither imported nor built. roadmap/roadmap.toml (modified), lean-benzecri/campaign/T-bz-c2-theoreme-affine/ and lean-benzecri/scaffold/BenzecriScaffold/{Applications,Chapter2}/ appeared while this audit ran. They belong to the atlas loop, not to this closer.

findings.what: The proposal replaces Causal.isCauchyInclusion_iSup by 'Causal.Causality.isCauchySurfaceOn_iSup and Causal.Causality.causallyConvexIn_of_isCauchySurfaceOn, the two lemmas used', and it adds globallyHyperbolicOn_sSup_of_pieces. But none of the three 4.63 anchors uses isCauchySurfaceOn_iSup. Its only use is ErsUnions.lean:210, inside isCauchySurfaceOn_sSup_of_curvesExtendOn. That lemma's only user is globallyHyperbolicOn_sSup_of_pieces, and no declaration uses that one. The anchors run through three other lemmas. The first is isCauchySurfaceOn_sSup_of_isAcausalOn, via isDevelopmentIn_localDevelopmentUnion. The second is IsCauchySurfaceOn.eq_of_le. The third is IsCommonDevelopment.globallyHyperbolicOn, which uses causallyConvexIn_of_isCauchySurfaceOn and GloballyHyperbolicOn.of_causallyConvexIn, and which the 4.63 list omits. Dropping isCauchyInclusion_iSup is right: there is no common Cauchy-included A, because each DS_p has its own S_p.
findings.fix: For 4.63, list ers_prop_4_63, ers_prop_4_63_globallyHyperbolicOn, ers_prop_4_63_of_hasTimeFunction and IsCommonDevelopment.globallyHyperbolicOn. As the library lemmas used, list causallyConvexIn_of_isCauchySurfaceOn, GloballyHyperbolicOn.of_causallyConvexIn and IsCauchySurfaceOn.eq_of_le. Cite globallyHyperbolicOn_sSup_of_pieces and isCauchySurfaceOn_iSup as the parallel union form, not as lemmas used.

findings.what: Applied as written, the localisation proposals fail tools/binder.py check. 4.63 gains globally_hyperbolic, causally_arc_connected and curves_extend, and 4.75 gains globally_hyperbolic and tarentin. Their only geometric entries (quasilinear, by T-loc-quasilinear-slice) have proves = [], and the open_localisation lists do not name these properties. binder.py would report each one as 'provided by no geometric entry and not declared open'. Three smaller points. (a) The corrected 4.63 note says only 'GH is proved by causal convexity'. It should give the hypotheses under which it is proved: S Cauchy in U₁, CausallyArcConnectedOn U₁ and CurvesExtendOn U₁. (b) Row 4.64's addition, 'V₀ GH under causally_arc_connected and curves_extend', also needs S Cauchy in U₁ (hS of IsCommonDevelopment.globallyHyperbolicOn). ers_theorem_4_64 does not assume it: it reads U₁'s Cauchy property as IsAcausalOn, SplitBy and CompactSlabs. (c) Row 4.77 binds the same added causality of the union as localisation is_causal, with a quasilinear supplier (:363). The 4.75 proposal leaves hcaus as prose under open_localisation.
findings.fix: Either add proves = [...] by T-loc-quasilinear-causal-ladder, as rows 4.64 and 4.67 do, or list the properties in open_localisation with a reason. State the three hypotheses in the 4.63 note, and S Cauchy in U₁ in the 4.64 addition. Bind 4.75's hcaus as is_causal, as in row 4.77. The curator decides.

findings.what: The REPORT calls the causality of U '(not printed)' and gives its supplier as 'none in ERS'. It is printed, as part of the conclusion: U is a GHD (:1021), so it is GH, so it is causal (:814). ers_theorem_4_75 therefore assumes part of what the paper concludes: it proves 'U causal for g(v) ⇒ S Cauchy in U'. It is disclosed as added and the row is partial, so the mark is not wrong. But the disclosure should say which part of the conclusion is assumed.
findings.fix: Write: '⚠ strengthened: ≤_U antisymmetric, a part of the paper's conclusion (U is a GHD) assumed, as in ers_theorem_4_77 (hcaus, OQ-41 (d))'.

findings.what: True, but two points could mislead the author. (i) It says the pieces 'do not give GH either, which follows from V being causally convex in the GH U₁'. In ERS's Lorentzian setting, GH of V follows from S being a Cauchy hypersurface of V (Geroch). So the ambient is used once, for the uniqueness of the meeting. Convexity is the ETT route, because Geroch (iii) ⇒ (i) is unproved there. (ii) The sharpness model cited has S = {0, 1}, which is disconnected, while ERS's S is connected (:814). The 4.75 finding says so; this one does not.
findings.fix: Write 'GH then follows (Lorentzian: from the Cauchy property, by Geroch; in ETT, without Geroch: from causal convexity in the GH U₁)', and say that the example is in 1+0 dimensions with S disconnected.

findings.what: The finding says 'its connected 2+1 analogue would be the winding hypersurface of ghd_02_19.tex:930'. That analogue is not formalised, and it lies outside ERS's construction. There W_p ⊆ T (:1011), where T is the image of the flow Φ of N, a diffeomorphism from D ⊆ ℝ × S, and N is timelike on DS_p. So, by ERS's own argument at :1014, the integral curve through a point of DS_p ∩ DS_q meets S once, in S_p ∩ S_q. Local developments on adjacent sheets of the winding surface therefore cannot overlap. As a remark on 'local developments alone' it is plausible. Sent to the author without that qualifier, it could read as a failure of ERS's construction, which it is not. The rest of the finding is true: the property is asserted without argument, and the claim's by-product supplies it, with 4.77's argument and the added causality of U.
findings.fix: Add 'outside ERS's construction, which the flow tube T excludes', or drop the sentence.

findings.what: RestartsIn.stay is FrontierStaysIn. Its roadmap supplier is T-loc-quasilinear-frontier (programme/roadmap.toml:1023, and the geometric by of binder row 4.64), not T-loc-quasilinear-slice. Both targets' titles state their hypothesis for W = U₁, L = U₁ ∩ U₂ and common developments. RestartsIn asks for them with W = DS_p, L a component of DS_p ∩ DS_q and IsDevelopmentIn, plus Prop 4.63's local uniqueness on S ∩ A. The REPORT raises this for SliceRestart only.
findings.fix: Name T-loc-quasilinear-frontier as the supplier of stay. Put the component-located forms to the planner as a scope question for both T-loc targets.

findings.what: (i) The SCOPE bullet title 'Prop 4.63 in full' (:74) reads as a certification claim on an unmarked partial row; the sentence after it means 'the full conclusion'. (ii) The checklist writes '⚠ added' (:64, :68) where kb/0006 has '⚠ strengthened'. (iii) The checklist has no row for the standing hypotheses: S connected (:814; unused, so a weakening), ℝ^{d+1} read as [T2Space M] [LocallyConnectedSpace M], and β nonempty. (iv) The REPORT calls ers_prop_4_63's IsAcausalOn U₁ S 'weakened'. In ETT it is a reading (OQ-41), not a weakening of 'S Cauchy in U₁': getting acausality from the Cauchy property needs CausallyArcConnectedOn and CurvesExtendOn (IsCauchySurfaceOn.eq_of_le). The REPORT also says no connectedness is 'printed in 4.63'. That is true of the statement, but the standing assumption at :814 prints it.
findings.fix: Write 'Prop 4.63's full conclusion' and '⚠ strengthened'. Add a row for the standing hypotheses. Call IsAcausalOn U₁ S a 'reading (OQ-41)', and cite :814 for S connected.

findings.what: The consequence is recorded 'at globally_hyperbolic', but its witness globallyHyperbolicOn_sSup_of_pieces never assumes Causal.Causality.GloballyHyperbolic, the node's lean form. It assumes GloballyHyperbolicOn B and the relative forms. The note says this itself, and also says that the case B = ⊤ is the existing pair causallyConvexIn_of_isCauchySurfaceOn + GloballyHyperbolicOn.of_causallyConvexIn. ladder.py only resolves the name, so the entry would pass its check, but it would sit among the M-level consequences of the node. The 4.63 anchors also do not use this lemma (finding 1).
findings.fix: Keep it as the proposed kb pattern, or record the B = ⊤ instance. The keeper decides.
